questions.q: Using the method 'Development as Political Contestation', work with: group_interests_weighted = 20, political_approval = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of development_decision.

Take the relation taught for 'Development as Political Contestation' and work with: group_interests_weighted = 15, political_approval = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of development_decision.
Explain in your own words what 'Development as Political Contestation' refers to.
questions.a: Decisions about development are not technical puzzles that experts alone can settle: building a steel plant on tribal iron-ore land weighs one social group's livelihood against another's, the present against the future, and jobs against environment -- so in a democracy the final call belongs to elected representatives, not to markets or experts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Development as Political Contestation'.
questions.a: Whose need counts as the nation's need is itself a political question; every development choice creates winners, losers and a legitimate debate.

concepts.title: Ideas of Development: Modernisation and Two Rival Models

questions.q: Using the method 'Ideas of Development: Modernisation and Two Rival Models', work with: liberal_capitalist_model = 80000, socialist_model = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of development_models.

Take the relation taught for 'Ideas of Development: Modernisation and Two Rival Models' and work with: liberal_capitalist_model = 50000, socialist_model = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of development_models.
Explain in your own words what 'Ideas of Development: Modernisation and Two Rival Models' refers to.
questions.a: Post-Independence debate treated development as becoming modern, usually measured against the industrialised West, but India stood before two ready-made routes: the liberal-capitalist model of Europe and the US and the socialist model of the USSR; with communists, socialists and Nehru alike impressed by Soviet growth, the socialist model had the stronger following and left meant state control while right meant free markets.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ideas of Development: Modernisation and Two Rival Models'.
questions.a: Development is an idea with politics inside it -- which model you pick decides who owns industry and who answers for redistribution.

concepts.title: Planning, the Planning Commission and the Bombay Plan

questions.q: Using the method 'Planning, the Planning Commission and the Bombay Plan', work with: bombay_plan_heritage = 50, five_year_plans = 100, planning_commission_1950 = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of planning_apparatus.

Take the relation taught for 'Planning, the Planning Commission and the Bombay Plan' and work with: bombay_plan_heritage = 25, five_year_plans = 50, planning_commission_1950 = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of planning_apparatus.
Explain in your own words what 'Planning, the Planning Commission and the Bombay Plan' refers to.
questions.a: Because development could not be left to private actors, India set up a Planning Commission in March 1950 by a simple government resolution -- not by the Constitution -- with the Prime Minister as chairperson and an advisory role whose plans needed Cabinet approval; the impulse crossed political lines, as shown by the Bombay Plan of 1944 in which big industrialists themselves asked the state to lead industrial investment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Planning, the Planning Commission and the Bombay Plan'.
questions.a: From left to right, planning was the obvious choice: even industrialists wanted the state to take the major economic initiatives.

questions.q: Using the method 'Five Year Plans and the Plan-Non-Plan Budget Divide', work with: non_plan_expenditure = 25, plan_expenditure = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of annual_budget.

Take the relation taught for 'Five Year Plans and the Plan-Non-Plan Budget Divide' and work with: non_plan_expenditure = 25, plan_expenditure = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of annual_budget.
Explain in your own words what 'Five Year Plans and the Plan-Non-Plan Budget Divide' refers to.
questions.a: Indian planning copied the Soviet device of five year plans: a document fixing government income and expenditure for five years, with budgets split into a non-plan part for routine yearly spending and a plan part spent on five-year priorities; excitement peaked with the Second Plan of 1956 and faded by the Fourth, when crisis forced a plan holiday in 1966.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Five Year Plans and the Plan-Non-Plan Budget Divide'.
questions.a: The five-year horizon let government act on the larger picture, but plan enthusiasm could not survive the economic crisis of the mid-1960s.

concepts.title: First Plan versus Second Plan: Agriculture First or Industry First

questions.q: Using the method 'First Plan versus Second Plan: Agriculture First or Industry First', work with: agrarian_first_plan = 300, industrial_second_plan = 75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of strategy_shift.

Take the relation taught for 'First Plan versus Second Plan: Agriculture First or Industry First' and work with: agrarian_first_plan = 4, industrial_second_plan = 360. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of strategy_shift.
Explain in your own words what 'First Plan versus Second Plan: Agriculture First or Industry First' refers to.
questions.a: The First Plan (1951-1956) preached patience -- K. N. Raj's hasten slowly -- concentrating on dams, irrigation and land reform to revive agriculture hit by Partition; the Second Plan (1956), drafted under P. C. Mahalanobis after the Avadi resolution on a socialist pattern of society, chased rapid industrialisation through heavy industry, import tariffs and a dominant public sector, but bred foreign-exchange strain, food worries and an urban bias.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'First Plan versus Second Plan: Agriculture First or Industry First'.
questions.a: The first plan guarded rural livelihoods while the second gambled on structural transformation, and the tension between feeding people and building factories never fully disappeared.
